descs: Reed and black water, gray on gray, and the smell of standing water.

spots.name: The Sunk Fence
spots.desc: Fence posts march into black water and keep going under it, some farmer's boundary from before the fen took this ground.

spots.name: Dike's End
spots.desc: The ground firms and rises toward a dike; north, drier land climbs on toward Hollowbrook. South, the fen closes back in.

actions.label: read the ground
fx: Bootprints press deep here, then vanish onto the dike's stone. Someone crosses this way often, and lightly.

spots.name: Eel-Trap Row
spots.desc: A dozen woven eel-traps hang from a rope strung between posts, half of them torn open and empty.

variants.desc: A dozen woven eel-traps hang from a rope strung between posts, half of them torn open and empty. Word's reached even here: new nets may go in over the burned nave before the season turns.
variants.brief: Torn traps. Talk of new nets on the burned water.

spots.name: Widow's Weir
spots.desc: A stone weir, moss-slick, channels the black water into a chattering fall barely a foot high. Someone still maintains it, badly.

spots.name: Rush Bank
spots.desc: Rushes taller than a man crowd the bank, cut through by a single narrow track of trodden mud. Wild mint grows rank where the ground stays drier.

spots.name: Sunken Howe
spots.desc: A low mound breaks the reed-flat, turf grown thick and dark. A black doorway shows in its flank, half-choked with silt.

actions.label: read the drag-marks
fx: Reed is crushed flat in a line from the doorway, out and back, more than once. Whatever uses this door, it comes and goes.

spots.name: Drowned Orchard
spots.desc: Fruit trees stand dead to the waist in black water, bare branches holding their shape years after the roots gave up on it.

spots.name: The Reed-Cutter's Camp
spots.desc: A one-room hut on a spit of drier ground, reed bundled in stacks outside it taller than the roof itself.

actions.label: count the reed-stacks
fx: More reed cut and bundled than one hut could use in a year. Whoever lives here doesn't stop, or doesn't sleep much.

spots.name: Heron Reach
spots.desc: A line of herons stands in the shallows, so still you take them for dead branches until one of them blinks.

actions.label: raid a heron's catch — 1hp risk (grace)
fx: You lift a fat eel clean out of a heron's beak before it knows you're there. It does not forgive you for it.
A heron's beak finds your knuckles before your fingers find the fish. The whole line takes wing, screaming.

spots.name: The Last Dry Ground
spots.desc: Reed gives way to firm footing here; west the ground rises dry toward the causeway and the Vale beyond it. East, only water.

spots.name: Mudflat Crossing
spots.desc: A stretch of gray mudflat, pocked with footprints going every direction, none of them recent.

actions.label: search the crossing (wits)
fx: One set of prints doubles back on itself, pressed deeper than the rest. Someone dropped a purse here, and never came back for it.
The footprints lead everywhere and nowhere. Whatever this crossing has seen, it isn't giving it up today.

spots.name: The Drowned Nave's Roof
spots.desc: A chapel roof breaks the black water like a whale's back, moss-slick and cracked open along the ridge. Something under it hums, low, just past hearing.

actions.label: listen to the roof
fx: The hum comes up through the slates, felt in your teeth more than heard. It doesn't stop when you do.

spots.name: Bell-Rope Reeds
spots.desc: Reeds grow unnaturally straight here, in a ring, as if something below keeps them that way. The water at the center never quite goes still.

variants.desc: Reeds grow unnaturally straight here, in a ring, as if something below keeps them that way. You already have a name to give the water, if you can find your way back to it.
variants.brief: The ring of reeds. A name still unspoken.

spots.name: Stilt-Shadow
spots.desc: Reedholm's roofs show east through the reeds, close now, nets strung rail to rail between the houses.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: From Stilt-Shadow: the drowned nave, two stands west; the Eel-Run, one west then one south; Sunken Howe, three west then one north; the causeway, four stands west.

spots.name: Cairn in the Reeds
spots.desc: A cairn of flat stones, half sunk, older than anything else standing in this fen. No one has left an offering here in a long time.

spots.name: The Flood-Watch
spots.desc: A stone tower leans but holds, the only thing in the fen taller than the reeds. Its door hangs open on one hinge.

actions.label: duck the loose door — 1hp risk (grace)
fx: The door swings on its one hinge and you're through before it decides to fall.
The door picks its moment and swings hard into your shoulder as you pass.

spots.name: The Long Gap
spots.desc: Open water stretches wide here, the reed line broken clean through, as if something once dragged a great weight across it.
spots.brief: A wide break in the reeds.

actions.label: look for what made this gap
fx: Reed is torn out by the root in a line too straight for wind or water. Something heavy came through here, and not long ago.

spots.name: The Eel-Run
spots.desc: The bank here is undercut, a black opening low over the waterline, wide enough to duck into if the water's low.

actions.label: listen at the bank
fx: Something breathes, slow and even, just past where the dark starts. It hasn't noticed you yet, or doesn't care to.

spots.name: Trapper's Blind
spots.desc: A hunter's blind of woven reed, collapsed at one corner, aimed out over water where nothing has moved in years.
onEnterOnce: This is Fenmarch: the fen where the water rose in a night twenty years gone and took the old nave, congregation and all.

spots.name: The Milestone
spots.desc: A stone marker leans in the mud, its carved word worn past reading. Whatever it once pointed toward, the fen has swallowed the road as well as the name.

actions.label: trace the worn carving
fx: Half a word survives under your fingers, more guess than reading. It might have once said REEDHOLM. It might have said something older.

spots.name: Cutter's Path
spots.desc: A narrow path of laid reed-bundles, sunk half into the mud, the only dry footing for a long stretch either way.

spots.name: Shingle's Edge
spots.desc: Reed gives way to shingle underfoot, salt cutting through the standing water smell. South, a road climbs toward the coast.

actions.label: sift the tideline — 1hp risk (grace)
fx: You catch a glint before the next wave takes it back, and come up with coin, cold and green with age.
A wave takes your footing along with whatever you were reaching for.

spots.name: Gull Roost
spots.desc: Gulls have taken over a stand of dead trees, screaming at nothing in particular. Their droppings have killed what little green was left.

onEnter: Something surfaces beside you, gray and dripping, before you've even heard it move.

vars.NAME: Sunken Howe
vars.SIGN: Reed-marks scar the doorstone where something dragged itself out, and back in.

vars.NAME: The Reed-Cutter's Hut
vars.SIGN: Dried eels hang in a row from the rafters, twine looped through their eyes.
vars.VOICE: Eels don't ask, and I've grown used to that.

vars.NAME: The Flood-Watch
vars.VIEW: the whole fen spreads flat and gray, Reedholm's roofs east and the coast a pale line south
vars.SIGN: Flood-lines ring the tower's foot in bands, one for every bad year on record.

vars.NAME: The Eel-Run
vars.BEAST: a fen-eel thick as a leg
vars.SIGN: A trail of slime and dragged reed leads back into the dark, still wet.

fd_bog_hide.name: a strip of bog-thing hide
fd_bog_hide.hint: the eel-trader might pay to know what's tearing up her traps

fd_herbs.name: fen-mint, gathered wild
fd_herbs.hint: eat it to ease a wound

fx: Bitter and sharp. It clears the head and eases the ache.

fd_cairn_ward.name: a corroded ward-coin
fd_cairn_ward.hint: old, and worth something to the right buyer

fd_fence_latch.name: a corroded iron latch
fd_fence_latch.hint: torn from a gate the fen swallowed whole

fd_orchard_apple.name: a withered orchard apple
fd_orchard_apple.hint: shrunk hard as a stone, but sound

fx: Tough and sour, but it holds. Whatever kept these trees fruiting this long, it wasn't the roots.

fd_tally_stick.name: a drover's notched tally-stick
fd_tally_stick.hint: someone's count of a debt, lost before it was settled

fd_eelline.name: a coil of good eel-line
fd_eelline.hint: salvage; worth mending a trap or two

fd_ring_stone.name: a stone worn perfectly round
fd_ring_stone.hint: smooth all over, like the water shaped it on purpose

fd_old_arrowhead.name: a corroded arrowhead
fd_old_arrowhead.hint: nothing has moved here in years; this is likely why

fd_whetstone.name: a dropped whetstone
fd_whetstone.hint: worn to a curve; a reed-cutter's, most likely

fd_bog_thing.name: bog-thing
fd_bog_thing.desc: Gray-hided and too many-jointed, dripping black water, more animal than anything with a name. It hits like the bog itself closing over you, and does not tire.
onDeath: It comes apart into mud and old gray hide before it even finishes falling. One piece of hide holds its shape.

fd_weir_keeper.name: the weir-keeper
fd_weir_keeper.desc: Elbow-deep in the sluice, one hand always testing the flow.

topics.label: why keep a weir nobody thanks you for
topics.say: Fen floods without it. Reedholm only remembers that the year it does.

topics.label: ask what the weir needs
topics.say: Stone, mostly, and someone fool enough to keep coming back. Reeds don't fix themselves.

topics.label: the water's tithe, since you heard
topics.say: Heard about that, even out here. A tithe's just another toll the water charges. I've paid mine for years, in upkeep.

fd_beachcomber.name: a beachcomber
fd_beachcomber.desc: Turns over gull-killed ground with a stick, unbothered by the noise.

topics.label: what are you hunting for
topics.say: Whatever the gulls turn up and don't want. You'd be surprised what a dead tree collects, this far out.

topics.label: ask what they've found lately
topics.say: A little, this week. Take it — no use for coin out here with nothing to spend it on.
